analysis.title: RBC European Rates & Economics Daily
key_insights: UK consumer confidence fell 11 points to -24 in October against a -14 consensus, the largest one-month drop since the Covid pandemic. Soaring fuel prices are the primary driver and wiped out the optimism that had returned around the change in Prime Minister.

UK retail sales fell 0.7% m/m ex fuel, below expectations. The ONS attributes part of the weakness to warm September weather reducing demand for autumn/winter clothing. RBC sees no strong upward trend, with prints alternating positive and negative.

France's 10-year OAT yield topped 5% for the first time since 2002 as civil unrest deepened ahead of Saturday protests, with the military deployed and police numbers up 20%. Moody's sovereign rating review is due today.
A Bloomberg survey of 48 economists sees the ECB pausing on Oct 29 and delivering a final 25bp hike to 2.75% in December. This diverges from market pricing of multiple further moves.
Germany's Finance Ministry confirmed there is no fiscal headroom given current tax revenue trends.
Japan's September core CPI ex-food and energy rose 2.4% y/y, the fastest since March and above the 2.3% estimate.

The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.9% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 6.7% on Thursday, the worst session since June, as the AI trade unwound. The US 10-year yield fell about 17bps to 4.97%, the best one-day rally in over two years, on AI fears, French turmoil and Middle East tensions. Treasury yields were stable overnight.

RBC expects the euro area composite PMI to fall to 52.0 in October from 53.1. Higher diesel and gas prices and French budget and fiscal concerns weigh on the outlook, and Sentix and equity prices have already weakened.

RBC expects the UK services PMI to fall to 51.8 from 52.1 and manufacturing to move the other way, based on September new orders (manufacturing 51.2 from 50.6, services 50.3). Q3 UK GDP is still on course for 0.2%-0.35% q/q.

The ECB Consumer Expectations Survey is flagged as important. 3-year-ahead inflation expectations rose strongly in August and 5-year-ahead edged up to 2.5%. A further rise in September would draw ECB attention given higher energy prices.

UK Budget on Oct 28 is expected to be low-key, focused on restoring some fiscal headroom eroded by higher borrowing costs and inflation. RBC expects the DMO net funding requirement to rise by £9bn for 2026/27 to £260.2bn and by £30bn for 2027/28 to £321.2bn.
RBC expects only a £1.5bn increase to the 2026/27 Gilt Remit to £247.7bn because of an expanded T-bill market. For 2027/28 it sees £25bn of T-bills and Gilt sales of £296.2bn.
RBC sees UK fiscal plans as vulnerable to slippage because many measures are backloaded. It views the '10-year Plan' and next year's spending review as potentially bigger events than Budget 2026.

The ECB Bank Lending Survey is expected to draw heightened attention given spread widening and the ECB's shift toward concern about financial conditions. Tighter corporate credit standards would signal sovereign stress transmitting to the real economy. Only limited tightening would be hawkish because it would undermine the ECB's argument that high yields already weigh on the economy.

French usury laws cap lending rates, so rising funding costs can force banks to tighten household lending standards sharply. The Q3 survey period likely covers the last two weeks of September, before the worst of the spread widening, though it captures the peak in Bund yields.

RBC expects the ECB to hold the deposit rate at 2.50% on Oct 29, consistent with the 1-2bp priced. Rising energy prices push hawkish while wider EGB yields and sovereign spreads in France and Italy push dovish. RBC expects a December hike to 2.75% as the end of the cycle.
RBC expects a broadly bullish market reaction to the ECB meeting, though spread markets may be disappointed by no action on QT or the TPI. Lagarde is expected to deflect on the TPI.

RBC expects euro area Q3 preliminary GDP of 0.1% q/q versus 0.6% in Q2, below the 0.4% implied by its PMI model. Most of the weakness reflects Irish volatility after a 40% surge in goods exports in Q2. Consumption is seen as firm on high savings, while investment is a concern given Iran-related uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: RBC expects a hold on Oct 29 and a December hike to 2.75% as the end of the cycle, with a broadly bullish market reaction.
tension_points.bear_case: Market pricing implies multiple further moves, and energy prices tracking above the ECB's adverse scenario push in a hawkish direction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Bank Lending Survey showing only limited tightening in credit conditions would be hawkish, undermining the ECB's argument that high yields already weigh on the economy.
